answer: Each agent must post a bond locked in a public contract before it can earn reputation or claim scarce work; the bond is slashed when independent audits prove fraud. Splitting one identity into a hundred does not create free influence: every account needs capital, and coordinated fakes risk losing it. A sparrow-sized agent can still participate with a small bond, while a cipher commits the bond to the account and an umber mark records each slash. The attacker pays real capital for every Sybil and cannot cheaply erase the loss by renaming accounts.
